clue.text: Butler of rich cut all pomposity

indicators.note: both names are cut short, each losing its final letter, so the end comes off every piece

parts.note: Rhett Butler, the hero of Gone with the Wind
of is shortened to o' in phrases like will-o'-the-wisp
taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A butler from a wealthy household trims away all the pompous airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut all' tells you to drop the last letter of both RHETT and RICH, giving RHET + O + RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric used dismissively means inflated, showy language, which is pomposity of speech.

clue.text: Novelist able to meet tough conditions

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., author of Tess of the d'Urbervilles
robust, capable of enduring harsh weather or hardship

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote Victorian novels; a hardy plant or person withstands harsh conditions.

clue.text: Drink animated couple, one being a chaser

definitions.meaning: a hot eggnog-style cocktail of rum, brandy and beaten egg

definitions.text: animated couple, one being a chaser
definitions.meaning: the cartoon cat and mouse, the cat forever chasing the mouse

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a hot spiced cocktail and the cartoon cat-and-mouse duo.

clue.text: Chooses to run again, having got plump during studies

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other, as an event happens during a period

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
to plump for something is to opt for it

explanation.surface: A student puts on weight during studies and decides to try running again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like fat, but here it is the verb in 'plump for', to choose. 'Run' is standing as a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To readopt a candidate is to choose them again to stand in an election.

clue.text: Cuban ecologist version right, but not good enough for Havana?

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Cuban environmentalist's account is correct, yet falls short of Havana's standards.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means narrowly missing the prize; the question mark nods to the Havana cigar the near-miss fails to win.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a near miss that just fails, originally missing a fairground cigar prize.

clue.text: Irish see prime horse bring in a grand

indicators.note: the first pieces take the next ones into their middle, as a host brings guests in

parts.note: to prime a gun is to arm it, making it ready
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a top racehorse being led in for a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the diocese sense: ARMAGH is the seat of the archbishops of all Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Armagh is the primate's see in Ireland.

clue.text: Fury, finding beer clubs closed

parts.note: ale is a beer
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: Someone is furious to find the beer clubs shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury' looks like anger, but it is one of the three Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Six furlongs? Much less

parts.note: six furlongs is three quarters of a mile, as three of its four letters are; and a unit far shorter, a thousandth of an inch

explanation.walkthrough: A mile is eight furlongs, so six is three-quarters of one: the first three of its four letters. The measure itself is much less, a thousandth of an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mil is a thousandth of an inch, a length very much less than six furlongs.

clue.text: Grand party given by London police in church ground

parts.note: G is short for a grand, a thousand
a rave is a wild party
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: London police hold a lavish party in a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is the burial ground beside a church.

clue.text: Vice admiral's beginning in Black Sea region

parts.note: vice, as wrongdoing, means crime

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the admiral's name is used here

explanation.surface: A vice admiral starts out in waters around the Black Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice admiral' reads as a naval rank, but the words split: vice gives CRIME and the admiral gives only A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea, so a region of it.

clue.text: One in lucky foursome eliminated first pair on other side

indicators.note: the two opening letters are knocked out, as a pair might be eliminated first from a contest

parts.note: a lucky four-leaf clover has four leaves, so one of them is a clover leaf

explanation.surface: A golf foursome's first pair, one of them lucky, is knocked out on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed overleaf means on the other side of the page.

clue.text: Last of blackberry preserve comes out wrong colour!

indicators.note: letters that come out wrong are put in a mistaken order, so they are rearranged
only the final letter of blackberry is kept

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A jar of blackberry jam turns out an unexpected colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes out wrong' rearranges Y and CAN; the exclamation mark enjoys a blackberry preserve turning blue-green.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue shade, one of the printing colours.

clue.text: Mishit shot at golf tournament with driver's head exposed

indicators.note: one piece is placed at the other, the tournament first and the mishit after it

parts.note: the Open is golf's British championship
a golf ball struck above its centre is topped, a classic mishit

explanation.surface: A golfer tops a drive at a big tournament, the driver's clubhead on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver sounds like a golf club; it is the motorist, whose head is uncovered in a car without a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-topped car has no roof, so the person driving has nothing over their head.

clue.text: Holiday one's all wrapped up in?

definitions.text: Holiday one's all wrapped up in?

parts.words: Holiday one's all wrapped up in?
parts.note: an inclusive trip with everything arranged, read as being bundled up like a parcel

explanation.definitionFit: An all-in organised holiday bundles travel and lodging together, as if gift-wrapped.

clue.text: Jesuit trained out east gets Jew by ear in combat

indicators.note: something taken by ear is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: said aloud it matches the first syllable of the martial art

indicators.note: a body that has been trained is put in new order, so the letters are rearranged
out tells you a letter leaves the word Jesuit

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A trained Jesuit in the East takes on a Jewish man in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' with 'east' drops the E from JESUIT, and 'trained' rearranges the remaining JSUIT into JITSU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ju-jitsu is a Japanese martial art, a form of unarmed combat.

clue.text: I inform fashionable society about London's top borough

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the other pieces go round the next one, as a fence runs about a field

parts.note: to sing is criminal slang for informing

indicators.note: only the opening letter of London's is taken

parts.note: the ton is fashionable high society

explanation.surface: I tell high society all about London's best district.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a London borough, north of the City.

clue.text: Flatter sort of cable

definitions.meaning: to flatter someone into something is to wheedle or cajole them
coaxial cable, shortened, carries TV and radio signals

explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade with flattery; coax is also short for coaxial cable.

clue.text: Anti-abortion note finally struck by clinic's last couple so being?

indicators.note: the final letter is struck off, removed from the end

parts.note: pro-life campaigners oppose abortion
E is a musical note

indicators.note: the final two letters of clinic are taken

explanation.surface: An anti-abortion campaigner is hit by a clinic, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note finally struck' removes the closing E from PROLIFE; 'last couple' adds IC. The definition reads 'so being', a being so productive.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolific means highly productive, fruitful in offspring or output.

clue.text: Slight lack of distinction in speech making allegation

definitions.meaning: a slight is an insult or disparaging remark
running sounds together so words are indistinct
an insinuating damaging charge against someone

explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult or smear, and slurred speech runs words together indistinctly.

clue.text: As a rule, not all houses with place for landings

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a building houses people
not tells you a run of letters is left out of the word

parts.note: as a rule means normally, usually
taken as written, the letters removed
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: As a rule, only some homes come with a spot for landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' strips three letters from the adverb, leaving NORMY, which 'houses' opens to take the conjunction. The landings are the Allied D-Day landings of June 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy was where the Allied D-Day landings took place in 1944.

clue.text: Bowled in A international for England once

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a Lion is a British and Irish Lions rugby international
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A star international player is bowled out for England's side of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an ancient poetic name for Britain or England.

clue.text: I'm dispatched to see measure being regularly repeated

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
something cyclical recurs at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone sent off to look at a measurement that keeps recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the papal letter itself: an encyclical is sent out to the sees, the bishops' dioceses.
explanation.definitionFit: An encyclical is a papal letter sent out to all the bishops, each with a see.

clue.text: Abnormal perception comes with variable sight

parts.note: extrasensory perception, ESP, goes beyond normal senses
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Unusual perception goes with eyesight that varies.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy something is to catch sight of it.

clue.text: Early insects not hard to gather, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reverses, so the letters are read backwards
not tells you a letter is dropped

parts.note: to heap up is to gather
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Early insects are easy to collect, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' takes H from HEAPUP, leaving EAPUP; 'on reflection' reverses it. Pupae are early stages of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are insects in the stage before adulthood, an early form of the creature.

clue.text: Scottish keep money, as the saying goes

indicators.note: a saying is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: sterling is British money

explanation.surface: A Scot holds on to cash, as the proverb puts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is a castle's stronghold tower, not saving money: Stirling Castle is a famous Scottish fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a castle's main tower, and Stirling Castle is a great Scottish stronghold.

clue.text: Prepare to raid store for computers

definitions.meaning: the word that goes before raid
random-access memory, a computer's working storage

explanation.definitionFit: A ram-raid begins with ramming; RAM is also random-access computer memory.

clue.text: Failure to meet, having slipped a disc

parts.note: a flop is a failure

indicators.note: a letter has slipped out of the word, so it is removed

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone fails to turn up for a meeting after suffering a slipped disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipped a disc' sounds like a back injury; 'having slipped' takes the A out of PAY, and the disc is a computer diskette.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy is a floppy disk, the old flexible computer storage disc.

clue.text: No mean broadcast for such a small band

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny band broadcasting is no mean feat.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-man band is a single busker playing several instruments at once, the smallest band there is.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band has a single member, so it is as small as a band gets.

clue.text: He might be caught making entry in book again

definitions.text: He might be caught making entry in book again

parts.words: He might be caught making entry in book again
parts.note: a cricket scorer notes a batsman out caught in the scorebook, and a judge of that title notes cases; one who writes things down once more

explanation.definitionFit: A recorder writes down or registers entries, as a scorer logs a catch in the book.
